item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I love this story. It gave me new kinds of chills and explained some mysteries at the same time, which is exactly what I would want to see from SCP-001. (My favorite part is the careful structure of the initial excerpts referring to the Device, "finding a solution" and "replicating the technology", where you're set up to think that understanding 001-01 is the main goal being pursued by the writer.)

For a few minutes I actually thought that the scenario for which 001-34 was prepared (the Administrator's death and the passing of his duties to someone else) had actually taken place, possibly several times, and the most recent user of the Device is just the latest successor. This would even support the idea of the diary describing events in a Foundation that had to work to understand the Device- it sure looks like 001-34 and 001-35 are from the original Administrator's universe, and it's almost certain that 001-01 and 001-02 are… but we don't know that 001-03 is. It might just be the latest Administrator's Diary, having replaced previous versions that didn't survive.

(From the comments it sounds like this isn't the intent, which I find somewhat disappointing- this is a story about flawed people and their unsuccessful attempts to save the world; the idea that the Corruption has overrun tens of thousands of universes but never ever killed or even immobilized this one guy really clashes with that theme.)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Really don't understand why everyone is complaining about this article's length. There are far longer works on this site, and as long as a piece can keep me immersed and enthralled throughout (which it did), length isn't an issue.
That being said, while I do adore the premise and concept, the logs feel way too explain-y. When I used to write in my journal/diary, I would use really esoteric terms and abbreviations because it wasn't meant to be read by others, only myself. Here, it kinda feels like the Administrator is writing these entires with an audience in mind, and attempting to explain the events to them, rather than simply jotting down his/her thoughts. And if that is indeed the case, you'd think (s)he'd be way more explain-y.
Upvote anyways.

Have a lovely day!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The part I don't like: I'm somewhat confused how the note about us fighting away the darkness and being masters of our world really relates to the more explanatory note about the dimensional traveler and his device.

If you've read About the SCP Foundation and the Foundation's mission statement, it reveals to us that we're not the first one the Administrator told that particular lie. He's had to tell countless previous Foundations the same party line in an effort to keep them in line.

Also, the idea that an entire UNIVERSE (billions and billions of people on each planet, all working together) or maybe tens of thousands of universes would be willing to sacrifice their lives just to keep our universe alive seems utterly implausible (unless maybe they're significantly more compassionate than us asshole humans).

The Administrator's universe of origin was doomed. Faced with certain death, their species chose instead to try to save others from the same fate. Denizens of subsequent universes were… not so noble, hence the Administrator starting to lie about his mission.

I think there's a disconnect in understanding, here.

Hey guys, what if Mackenzie's Proposal was originally found with SCP-040?

The last letter indicated that he gave it to someone he loved, so it indicates that he gave it to either his daughter or wife, and since SCP-040's mutations often lead into new material being created, that must means that she subconsciously creates such material from something from her experience.

And the reason why she can't remember anything from her past is because she is disorientated from jumping from universe to universe trying to stop the corruption.

The part I don't like: I'm somewhat confused how the note about us fighting away the darkness and being masters of our world really relates to the more explanatory note about the dimensional traveler and his device.

item.title: Review
item.content:encoded: I would have to agree with all previous posts, that this SCP proposal is both a good and a bad one. While the story is excellent, leaving you to your own thoughts and imaginations, it is surrounded by just enough pointless details to seem drawn-out. Nonetheless, this is a mind-blowing concept and an interesting edition to the SCP universe…or universes…

item.content:encoded: Pay attention son. The device measures two things, the corruption level of the universe (23%), and the number of times the device was activated. That number is hidden, but it's in the ten's of thousands. meaning so far it's neither fixed things, nor shattered the universe. Theoretically meaning that all it's done is sped things along tens of thousands of times.
